basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 19.' and it opens '(Vers. 19.) Et fuit terminus Chananaeorum a Sidone, donec venias in Gerara usque ad Garam'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 19.) Et fuit terminus Chananaeorum a Sidone, donec venias in Gerara usque ad Garam pergentibus Sodomam, et Gomorrham, et Adamam, et Seboim usque ad Lise. Quia caeterae civitates, Sidon videlicet et Gerara, et Sodoma, et Gomorrha, et Adama, et Seboim notae sunt omnibus, hoc tantum annotandum videtur, quod Lise ipsa sit, quae nunc Callirhoe dicitur, ubi aquae calidae prorumpentes in mare Mortuum defluunt.
